name: Understand Anything
hook: 84.3k stars on the codebase knowledge graph tool still trending after its debut yesterday. Drop one JSON config in your repo and teammates get auto-generated guided tours ordered by dependency, semantic fuzzy search, and diff impact analysis that maps which system components any change actually touches. Multi-language output covers English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Spanish, and Turkish — skip re-analysis when your team or language changes.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 2 — 84.3k stars; Charlie Automates blog coverage surfacing in search results

name: PR Lens
hook: 1.7k stars on the PR visualization tool that posts animated architecture and data-flow walkthroughs inside each pull request. Dots cross arrows in execution order; click any arrow and the request/response shapes expand next to the graph. Runs as a GitHub App, GitHub Action, GitLab CI component, Bitbucket pipe, CLI, or Claude Code skill. Fills the gap Claude Code Review leaves: it shows what the whole change is, not just which line is wrong.

name: Magpie
hook: Menu bar app that routes Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode through a single shared subscription — switch providers and models without touching API keys or pausing your agent. Ships 50+ provider presets, MCP and skills management, usage profiles, and cross-agent credential sharing. Grew from 1.4k to 1.7k stars overnight on GitHub Trending as engineers discovered it cuts multi-agent subscription costs.

name: jevgrep
hook: Semantic code search CLI built for coding agents: describes files, functions, and interfaces in natural language instead of returning noisy raw line matches. The author benchmarks it at ~30% lower coding-agent cost from the reduced context overhead vs. grep or ripgrep. `jg skill` wires it into Claude Code so every search uses it automatically. 1.2k stars on its first appearance in GitHub Trending.
install: npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep && jg auth && jg skill

name: Agentic Awesome Skills (AAS)
hook: v18.7.0 ships 2,474 installable SKILL.md playbooks updated September 27 — the 47k-star cross-platform library's latest checkpoint. An agent-first control plane lets the agent discover, select, and validate its own skill stack without manual configuration. One install covers Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Kiro, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot, and Autohand Code simultaneously.

name: golive-skill
hook: Agent skill that takes whatever Claude Code just built to production. Detects your stack, proposes a deployment plan, waits for your approval, applies it, then verifies the result. Platform coverage: Vercel, Netlify, Supabase, Neon, Porkbun, Resend, and Stripe. No telemetry, MIT license, ~1k stars on its GitHub Trending debut.

name: agent-dispatch (DmitriyYukhanov/claude-plugins)
hook: v1.0.0 released September 26: label any GitHub issue `agent` and a scheduled tick fires `/issue-to-pr` headlessly on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Auto-resumes when you comment or re-label, pauses on rate-limits or logout, enforces a 4-hour timeout before yielding. Part of DmitriyYukhanov's claude-plugins bundle — install the whole bundle and get agent-dispatch plus the rest.

name: Claude-BugHunter
hook: 4.7k-star skill bundle for authorized security testing: 83 skills covering 58 vulnerability class patterns, all extracted from 681 publicly disclosed bug reports. Fifteen slash commands including `/hunt` for engagement scaffolding, enterprise platform coverage for M365/Entra, Okta, vCenter, and SSL VPN appliances, and Burp Suite MCP integration for interactive workflows. Built-in authorization and scope gates fire before any test begins.
